title: Find out whether a Forever motion shorter than the loop stutters
goal: Every motion in an icon shares one loop as long as the longest motion, and a motion that ends early holds still until the loop starts over. Reading the code says a spinner set to Forever at 800 ms beside a 900 ms bell pauses for a tenth of a second every turn, on the canvas and in the exported SVG, which breaks the promise that a spinner loops with no stutter. Check it, and if it is so, make a Forever motion repeat at its own pace.
notes: Not reproduced in the app: code reading only, hence p2 look-into. One shared cycle: Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerMotion.swift motionCycleLengthMS / automaticMotionCycleLengthMS ~1525-1550 (deliberately ONE CYCLE, see comment and MotionStrip.swift). A motion that ends early holds its final value (~1006). SVG export writes the same cycle length: Sources/PhotonzCore/SVGMotionExport.swift ~311; in SVG each animate element can carry its own dur with repeatCount=indefinite. Mock icon-loop-wt.html: 'with Forever on it, a length becomes a rate'.
acceptance: The case is run: one frame with a bell at its default 900 ms rotation and a spinner 0 to 360 degrees, Linear, Forever, 800 ms; the result (canvas and exported SVG in a browser) is written into this task's log with how it was measured
If the spinner pauses: a Forever motion repeats at its own length on the canvas and in the exported SVG, the timing strip shows that honestly, and a walk covers it at Next defaults
If it does not pause: the task closes with the evidence and no code change
Audit written under queue/audits/ if the app changed; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: REPRODUCED. Canvas: ForeverMotionPaceTests sampled value(atMS:) every 33 ms (preview rate) for bell = Add Rotation default (900 ms, there and back) + spinner 0->360 Linear Forever 800 ms: spinner stood still on frames 825, 858, 1716, 1749, 2607, 2640 ms (about 100 ms per turn). SVG: exported spinner was dur=900ms keyTimes=0;0.889;1 values=0;360;360. Browser: opened the exported file in Chrome, svg.pauseAnimations + setCurrentTime every 33 ms reading g.transform.animVal angle: 792->356.35, 825->360, 858->360, 891->360, 924->10.8, the same still frames [825,858,1716,1749,2607,2640].

FIX: MotionRepeat.keepsItsOwnPace (one way Forever only). LayerMotion.value(atMS:) waits for startMS once, then repeats every durationMS regardless of the lap. SVGMotionExport writes such a motion as its own turn: dur=durationMS, begin=startMS when late, keyTimes over its own span. Strip: MotionStripLane.turnMS + laterTurns(throughMS:), drawn as dashed quiet bars after the real one (MotionStripLaterTurns). After: the walk's exported SVG measured in Chrome the same way has no still frames (792->356.4, 825->11.25, 858->26.1). Tests that used .forever only to get a slide-then-hold now say .once (NestedMotionTests, MotionRenderTests), the lap-sharing SVG tests use there and back, DocumentTimeTests uses .times(4) to keep telling the two clocks apart.

left rough: Forever motions still count toward the automatic lap length, so a 1200 ms spinner beside a 900 ms bell makes the bell rest 300 ms per lap. Did not file: nobody has hit it, and whether a rate should set the lap is a design question for the per-turn readout task. Also: Forever there and back still shares the lap (rest at home, not a stutter). Video clips: a hand-set Forever now repeats every Over (new clip motions arrive as Once). Filed the-timing-strip-says-how-long-one-turn-of-a-for for the mock's '800 ms per turn' and 'ends where it starts' strip readouts. Audit: queue/audits/2026-10-15-forever-spinner-own-pace.json. I looked at 1-spinner-beside-bell-sc.png: the dashed later turn sits after the 800 ms bar and runs past the repeats line; the bell fills the 900 ms lap.
